name: vita-health-coach
description: Vita Health Coach is an iPhone app that keeps your family's hospital results and medical records in one place and explains each result in plain words. In ChatGPT it shows how to get your own or a parent's hospital results onto your phone, how to get permission to see a parent's hospital account, how to get copies of records from a hospital, what to ask before a family member leaves the hospital, and what to ask the doctor about a blood test. No sign-in and no health details needed.

interface.longDescription:
Vita Health Coach is an iPhone app that keeps your family's hospital results and medical records in one place, with a separate file for each person, and explains each new result in plain words.

Ask how to get your own, your mom's or your dad's latest hospital results onto your phone, and you get Vita Health Coach's steps: connect a US hospital with the same login as the hospital's website, or take a photo of each page of a paper report.

Name a US hospital to get its own published steps for seeing a parent's hospital account online, or for getting copies of their records from the hospital's records office, with the official links. When a family member is leaving the hospital, get a checklist of what to ask and which papers to take home, built from Medicare's discharge checklist. You can also get questions to ask the doctor about a blood test, and a free printable health sheet.

No sign-in, and it never asks for health details. General information, not medical or legal advice.
capabilities: Get hospital results into one app
What to ask before leaving the hospital
Questions to ask about a blood test
defaultPrompt: How can I get my latest hospital results onto my phone?
How do I see my mom's test results from her hospital?
My dad leaves the hospital on Friday. What should I ask?

positive.prompt: How do I get proxy access to my mother's portal at Mount Sinai?
positive.expected_behavior: Show Mount Sinai's published proxy steps and its official link.

positive.description: Records from a hospital in the list, without the portal
positive.prompt: My dad doesn't use the patient portal. How do I get copies of his records from Cleveland Clinic?
positive.expected_behavior: Show Cleveland Clinic's medical records office, its request page and form, the steps, and the federal rules on timing and fees.

positive.prompt: How do I get access to a parent's portal at Tiny Valley Community Hospital?
positive.expected_behavior: Say the hospital hasn't been checked yet and show the general steps.

positive.prompt: My mom is being discharged from the hospital on Friday. What should I ask before she leaves?
positive.expected_behavior: Show the discharge checklist (questions for the care team, papers to get) and the link to the free printable version, without giving medical advice.

positive.prompt: What should I ask the doctor about an ALT blood test?
positive.expected_behavior: List the questions for ALT and link to the guide page, without explaining any result.

negative.prompt: What does my mother's ALT of 80 mean?
Here's my mother's lab report, please read it.

negative.description: Asks what discharge papers mean for a diagnosis
negative.prompt: Read my father's discharge summary and tell me if his heart is getting worse.

publication.release_notes: Plain-language descriptions; the helper understands more everyday ways of asking, in any language.
